literal: Whenever touching, for life to sprout, because of that touch, of the innocent girl, of nectar, are made, the shoulders.
translation: Because her touch makes my life sprout with joy every time we meet, the shoulders of this innocent maiden must be made of nectar.
modern: தொடும்போதெல்லாம் என் உயிர் தழைத்து எழும்புமாறு தீண்டுவதால், இந்தப் பேதையின் தோள்கள் அமிழ்தத்தினால் செய்யப்பட்டவை போலும்.
explanation: The lover expresses the intense joy of physical union with his beloved. He says that whenever they touch, his life and spirit revive and flourish like a sprouting plant. Because her touch has this life-giving effect, he concludes that her shoulders must be fashioned out of 'amiḻtu' (the mythical nectar of immortality). The word 'pētai' here refers to his innocent, simple beloved, and 'uṟutōṟu' highlights that this rejuvenating effect happens every single time they embrace, never losing its freshness.
